systems.name: WordPress
systems.support: Free and open-source CMS maintained by the WordPress contributor community. Widely supported by commercial web hosting companies.
systems.technology: PHP server-side application using MySQL or MariaDB. Front end uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Apache or Nginx are commonly used web servers.
limitations: Plugins and themes must be kept updated
Third-party plugin quality can vary
Large numbers of plugins can increase maintenance and performance requirements
Security depends partly on keeping WordPress, themes, and plugins current

systems.name: Drupal
systems.support: Free and open-source CMS supported by the Drupal community and Drupal Association.
systems.technology: PHP-based CMS. Supports MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, and SQLite databases. Runs on Apache, Nginx, and other compatible web servers.
limitations: More configuration may be required than with simpler CMS platforms
Composer is commonly required for installation and updates
Modules can have additional PHP or configuration requirements
Major upgrades may require checking contributed module compatibility

systems.name: Joomla
systems.support: Free and open-source CMS supported by Open Source Matters and the Joomla community.
systems.technology: PHP-based CMS supporting MySQL, MariaDB, and PostgreSQL. Common web servers include Apache, Nginx, and Microsoft IIS.
limitations: Extensions and templates need compatibility checks during upgrades
Advanced customization may require PHP and Joomla-specific knowledge
Additional extensions can increase maintenance requirements
Server must meet supported PHP and database requirements

systems.name: Ghost
systems.support: Open-source publishing platform developed by the Ghost Foundation. It is available as self-hosted software or through the managed Ghost(Pro) service.
systems.technology: Node.js-based CMS. The recommended production stack uses Node.js, MySQL, Nginx, and Ubuntu Linux. Themes use HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Handlebars.
limitations: Primarily designed for publishing rather than general-purpose application development
Some advanced customizations require editing theme code
Self-hosting requires server administration
Headless implementations lose some built-in Ghost features unless they are recreated

systems.name: Strapi
systems.support: Open-source headless CMS developed by Strapi with community, cloud, and enterprise support options.
systems.technology: Node.js-based headless CMS. Supports SQLite, MySQL, MariaDB, and PostgreSQL databases. Content is normally delivered to a separate front end through APIs.
capabilities: Works with front-end frameworks such as React, Next.js, Vue, and others
limitations: Does not provide a traditional finished website front end
Developers must create or connect a separate presentation layer
NoSQL databases such as MongoDB are not supported in Strapi 5
Strapi does not support connecting applications directly to arbitrary pre-existing databases
